history.dynasty: Medieval Cholas; later contributions by the Vijayanagara Empire and the Madurai Nayaks
history.period: Significant antiquity; Chola-era core with Vijayanagara and Nayak additions
history.summary: One of the 108 Divya Desams, counted among the Pancharanga Kshetrams and the Pancha Kshethram temples, and one of Kumbakonam's landmark shrines. The rajagopuram has eleven tiers and rises 173 ft (53 m), the largest temple tower in Kumbakonam; the temple is enshrined within a huge granite wall with the Potramarai tank opposite the western entrance. Legend: sage Hema (Hemarishi) performed penance on the banks of the Potramarai tank and was blessed with a daughter, Lakshmi incarnate, who emerged from a lotus and was named Komalavalli; Vishnu descended from Vaikunta to woo and marry her, holding a bow (saranga) in his hand (pani) - hence Sarangapani. The moolavar is the reclining Aravamudhan under the Vaideeka Vimana. Because the Lord came here directly from Vaikunta, this Divya Desam has no Sorgavasal (the Vaikunta Ekadasi door common elsewhere). A well-known local tradition: the devotee Lakshmi Narayanaswami, who built the rajagopuram, was childless, and the Lord himself performed his last rites (Deepavali shraddha of Sri Lakshmi Narayanaswami, observed in Aippasi). Glorified in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham by seven Alvars including Tirumangai Alvar (25 pasurams) and Nammalvar. The twin temple chariots are among the largest in Tamil Nadu (about 300 tonnes base each). COORDINATE FLAG: map-pin-level geocode from the map tool - verify on the ground before treating as precise.

name: Sarangapani Temple
town_description: Kumbakonam, in Thanjavur district on the Cauvery river about 40 km from Thanjavur and 273 km from Chennai, is a historic temple town famed for its Mahamaham festival (held every 12 years) and dense cluster of Shaivite and Vaishnavite shrines.

travel.airport: Tiruchirappalli International Airport (TRZ), about 100 km away, is the nearest airport.
travel.railway: Kumbakonam Junction (KMU) on the Chennai-Tiruchirapalli line; the temple is in central Kumbakonam, a short auto/taxi ride from the station.
travel.road: Well connected by road to Chennai, Tiruchirappalli, Thanjavur and other south Indian cities; the temple sits on the town's main thoroughfares with the Potramarai tank opposite its western entrance.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; March-April for the Chithirai chariot festival.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 7:00 AM-12:00 noon and 5:00-9:00 PM (per indianpanorama and tamilwebworld); six daily rituals run from 5:30 AM to about 9:00 PM - verify before visiting.
